newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Maruti says recalling 50,000 cars.
newsitem.headline: India's Maruti says recalling 50,000 cars.

text.p: Leading Indian carmaker Maruti Udyog Ltd said on Saturday it planned to recall 50,000 cars sold between November 1996 and April 1997 after finding defective steering systems were installed in about 1,500 of them.

"This defective part has gone into a very small percentage of cars and we are recalling 50,000 cars made during a certain period," a Maruti spokesman told Reuters. "About 1,500 cars are expected to be defective."

The spokesman said the company would place an advertisement in Indian newspapers that would identify the cars by their chassis and engine numbers, and ask consumers to bring the vehicles back to the factory.
"Then we will check them. Whichever has a defective part, we will replace it free of cost," the spokesman said. "The estimate of the cost to us is still being worked out."
He said the defect was a metallurgical fault that originated in steering system components manufactured by India's Mukund Steel and supplied to Maruti by Sona Steering Systems Ltd.

Maruti is a 50-50 joint venture between the Indian government and Japan's Suzuki Motor Corp. It sold 338,690 vehicles in 1996/97 (April-March). Its 800-cc hatchback model commands more than 80 percent of the small car segment of India's automobile market.
